clue.text: County suit under discussion

indicators.note: something under discussion is being talked about, so the word is taken as spoken

parts.note: hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone wonders about a lawsuit being argued over in a county court.
explanation.walkthrough: HERTS is the usual short form of Hertfordshire, an English county north of London; said aloud it matches the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Hertfordshire, abbreviated in writing, is one of the home counties of England.

clue.text: Excellent thing, tea or coffee perhaps?

definitions.meaning: something impressive or first-rate is called ...
a playful literal reading: drinks served steaming

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for anything outstanding, and literally describes any steaming beverage.

clue.text: Little movement arising in actual performance

indicators.note: signals that one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: actual means real

indicators.note: in a down clue something arising goes upward, so the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: a tic is a small involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A slight gesture emerges during a genuine stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' signals an upward reading in this down clue; 'movement' suggests music, fitting the surface, but is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a concert or a solo musical show given before an audience.

clue.text: Witness jumpers being lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the word makes it read upward, so backwards

parts.note: tops are garments such as jumpers (sweaters)

explanation.surface: Someone sees sweaters being stolen or raised.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater; 'being lifted' turns TOPS upside down in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice or see it, as an onlooker does.

clue.text: Skill in fraud on its way

indicators.note: signals that one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick or swindle
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A clever con is under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the containment signal; the definition 'on its way' sits after the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A race or project that is starting has begun and is under way.

clue.text: Foreign words aimed at a Tuareg gal, gent translates

indicators.note: to translate is to turn into another form, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone directs foreign speech at a desert woman while a gentleman interprets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translates' shuffles A TUAREG GAL GENT; the Tuareg are a Saharan people.
explanation.definitionFit: In translation, the tongue a text is being rendered into is the one the translator aims for.

clue.text: Collar estimated, by the sound of it

indicators.note: says the word is taken as heard rather than as written

parts.note: a rough figure is an estimated one

explanation.surface: A neckpiece whose size was guessed, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruff is a large pleated frilled neckband worn in Elizabethan times.

clue.text: Break down in tears initially: see, I'm upset

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the words in and tears
upset means knocked over or disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone collapses crying, saying look, I'm distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the openings of 'in tears'; 'upset' rearranges SEE and IM into EMISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise a bill is to split it into its separate parts, listing each one.

clue.text: Bubbly guy gutted to admit halfwit

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside the other
a gutted word has lost its insides, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A cheerful man is devastated at having to let a fool in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' leaves G and Y from guy, and 'to admit' puts ASS between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizzy drinks full of bubbles are full of gas.

clue.text: Previously referred to a figure heard and acknowledged

indicators.note: signals that the number is taken as it sounds

parts.note: four is a number, a figure
to have mentioned something is to have acknowledged it in passing

explanation.surface: A number was spoken and recognised, as noted earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns FOUR into its sound-alike FORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal and formal writing uses this word for anything already named earlier in the text.

clue.text: Second rotten reprimand

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a second
food that is off has gone bad

explanation.surface: A second scolding for something gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a telling-off is a British idiom for scolding them.

clue.text: Beams following in empty rays

indicators.note: signals that one piece sits inside the other
an emptied word has lost its contents, keeping only its outside letters

parts.note: after means following

explanation.surface: Light beams come after empty rays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves R and S from rays, and 'in' puts AFTER between them. 'Beams' looks like rays of light but means timbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloping timbers holding up a roof are its main structural joists.

clue.text: Egyptian monarch with posh skirt

parts.note: Tut is short for Tutankhamun, the boy pharaoh
U is a label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A pharaoh is dressed in an upper-class skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina wears a short stiff skirt of layered netting.

clue.text: Sign there's tooth decay, first one pulled

indicators.note: the leading letter is pulled out, as a tooth would be

parts.note: caries is the medical word for tooth decay

explanation.surface: There are signs of decay, so the first tooth is extracted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first one pulled' drops the opening C of CARIES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ram is the first of the twelve zodiac signs.

clue.text: Large and neat

definitions.meaning: a ... sum of money is a sizeable one
neat means orderly and in its place

explanation.definitionFit: A considerable amount is called tidy, and a neat orderly room is too.

clue.text: Amount paid to secure a cruise

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece holds the other within

parts.note: the cost is the price paid

explanation.surface: Money spent to book a holiday at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' puts A inside COST. 'cruise' looks like a holiday at sea but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to move along easily without effort, like cruising.

clue.text: Part of church beginning to leak — something contemplated?

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of leak

explanation.surface: A section of a church has started leaking, worrying worshippers.
explanation.walkthrough: Navel-gazing is a phrase for self-absorbed contemplation, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Mystics are pictured meditating on the belly button, so it is a thing pondered.

clue.text: Do as I do facing queen: that's child's play!

parts.note: follow my lead is an instruction to copy me
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A command to copy someone in front of the queen, a trivial matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' just places the two pieces side by side; 'child's play' looks like 'easy' but names a children's game.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a children's game in which everyone copies the moves of whoever is at the front.

clue.text: Boss eats horribly toxic substance

indicators.note: horribly suggests something mangled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The boss eats something dreadfully poisonous.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibrous mineral was used for insulation until its dust was found to cause lung disease.

clue.text: Unpleasant sensation, those things coming to a point?

definitions.meaning: the tingling felt when a numb limb recovers

definitions.text: those things coming to a point?
definitions.meaning: literally, sewing tools that end in sharp points

explanation.definitionFit: The prickling in a limb returning to feeling is named after the sharp sewing implements.

clue.text: Stonier rocks coming soon

indicators.note: to rock is to shake about, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: More rocky ground is on its way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like a noun about stones but is the verb that rearranges STONIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in store awaits you in the near future.

clue.text: Stage before drive shows cricketing skill

indicators.note: puts the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
a spin is a short drive in a car

explanation.surface: One part of a journey comes before a motoring trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Leg spin is a style of bowling in cricket where the ball turns after bouncing.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg spin is a slow bowling technique in cricket, a craft of the wrist spinner.

clue.text: Tiniest bits of crumbs adorning squalid tool shed

indicators.note: the smallest bit of each word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A grubby garden hut is littered with crumbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like the tool hut but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake cast its skin, meaning it dropped or discarded it.

clue.text: Drink beginning to cheer up dad

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of cheer

parts.note: pa is a word for father

explanation.surface: A beverage begins to lift a father's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: A cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal word for a cup of tea names a hot drink.

clue.text: Irritation in summit that's audible

indicators.note: says the word is taken as heard

parts.note: a peak is a mountain top

explanation.surface: Annoyance at the top of a mountain can be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit of resentment from wounded pride is a moment of annoyance.

clue.text: Faint, not very fit

indicators.note: says the next piece is left out

parts.note: a faint memory is a vague one

explanation.surface: Someone feels dizzy and unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like 'healthy' but is a noun for a bout of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: An ague is a feverish attack of shivering, such as malaria brings.

clue.text: Take a punt on a Greek character

parts.note: to take a punt is British slang for having a bet

explanation.surface: Someone gambles on a person from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The second letter of the Greek alphabet follows alpha.

clue.text: Stair hamsters perhaps will climb

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing reads the word upward, so backwards

parts.note: hamsters are an example of household animals kept as companions

explanation.surface: Little rodents scramble up a staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will climb' turns PETS upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Each single tread of a staircase is one of these.

clue.text: Substance in meat to ripen bananas

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so these letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Something in meat makes bananas ripen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit but means mad, shuffling TO RIPEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat is rich in this nutrient, needed for building muscle.

clue.text: Decay — as might stew?

definitions.meaning: to deteriorate or go to ruin
literally, a stew is put into a cooking pot

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to deteriorate badly, and a stew literally ends up in a cooking vessel.

clue.text: Dodgy deal with assistant in Antipodean city

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: an aide is a helper or assistant

explanation.surface: A shady business deal with a helper takes place in an Australian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' rearranges DEAL into ADEL. 'Antipodean' means Australian or New Zealander.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the state capital of South Australia.

clue.text: Underwear of poor quality

definitions.meaning: British slang for rubbish or bad

explanation.definitionFit: The word means underpants in Britain, and is also slang there for something rubbish.
